response.answer: In 2026, the Musée de l’Orangerie will present "Monet: Painting Time" from September 2026 to January 2027 to commemorate the 100th anniversary of Monet’s death. Additionally, the Musée Marmottan Monet is offering "Histories of Landscapes: From Monet to Hockney (1890-2025)." Monet's water lilies, painted between 1897 and 1926, remain a significant focus in art history.

results.title: In France, Brutal Summer Heat Waves Are Taking a Toll on the Flowers That Inspired Claude Monet's Most Beloved Paintings
results.content:
2026 marks 100 years since Monet’s death.
 To commemorate the anniversary, the Musée de l’Orangerie is presenting “Monet: Painting Time” from September 2026 to January 2027. The Musée Marmottan Monet is offering “Histories of Landscapes: From Monet to Hockney (1890-2025).” [...] November 19, 2018

Sarah Kuta/ [...] However, “some foliage still burned,” Lecoutre tells France 3’s Medhi Weber, per a translation by ARTnews’ Devorah Lauter. “There are physiological phenomena happening at the plant level. They close their stomata, and they stop flowering. So we had a lot of wilted flowers.”

Looking ahead, the team is also considering adding more heat-resilient plant varieties, but it must balance the need to adapt to a changing climate with the garden’s original character.
